title: Parable XI
identity: Persichetti’s Parable XI, Op. 123, is a solo alto saxophone work commissioned by Brian Minor and premiered by him in Kalamazoo on 14 April 1973. A University of North Texas dissertation describes an ABA' design with a very fast, more articulated B section and a three-line cadenza; it reports a 2.5-octave span and several color techniques. Its duration differs across sources: a Persichetti work list gives 4:30, while the dissertation extraction appears to read approximately 7 minutes.

evidence.claim: Recording track listing includes Parable XI performed by alto saxophonist Brian Minor.

University of North Texas dissertation describes Parable XI as ABA' with changing meters and barlines, except for a three-line cadenza in the middle of B; A sections are slow and lyrical, B is very fast and articulated. It reports a 2.5-octave range, pitch bends, fast vibrato, and approximately ten requested tone colors. These are the dissertation's descriptions, not independent score observations.
evidence.source_name: University of North Texas doctoral dissertation on Persichetti’s Parables

evidence.claim: Dissertation discography lists three recordings of Parable XI: Brian Minor with Chicago Symphony String Quartet and Lawson Lunde (Crystal S-151), James Stoltie (Coronet LPS-3036), and Dale Underwood (Golden Crest RE-091). The audio was not auditioned.
evidence.source_name: University of North Texas doctoral dissertation discography

review_focus: Inference from the dissertation’s work-specific description: review contrast between slow lyrical A sections and the fast articulated B section, including pacing through the central cadenza and color changes.
